correctness.rationale: PASS. Retrieved frozen theorem, full verification code, metadata and scientific context. The geometric fixed-point orbit-simplex realization requires whole two-vertex translation orbits with equal barycentric coefficients; each orbit has diameter 2. At scale 2 opposite parity orbit types (p,z) have cross-distance 1+d(z,z'), while same type has max distance 2+d(z,z'), so edges are exactly group generators (1,0),(1,e_i) and no triangles. An invertible parity coordinate transform gives the (n−1)-cube graph, connected with stated cycle rank. The cube graph cycle lattice is generated by elementary 4-cycles; at scale 3 each is filled by two triangles or a four-triangle cone, so the integral H1 map is zero. Signed oriented-edge permutation modules plus regular vertex module give multiplicities m−|b| for first-bit-negative characters and |b|−1 for other nontrivial characters. n=2 gives a single interval and zero H1. Independently enumerated all translation orbits, compatible orbit edges, connectivity, triangle-free property and H1 rank for n=2..7 (six cases). Actual source verifier covers extra finite square fillings; script contents were inspected, not blindly accepted. The unrestricted statement uses the orbit and cycle-generation proofs, not bounded tests.
